 This miscellaneous appeal having been heard and re  orders, coming on for pronouncement this day, Justice Achal K  Paliwal pronounced the following  ORDER

This appeal by the claimants under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 28.10.2021 passed by Member MACT, Mandleshwar in Claim Case No.174/2019 seeking enhancement of compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal.
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal,
for the death of Himanshu, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.16,23,172/- along with interest.

The breakup of the compensation amount is as under:
Income of deceased Rs.9935/-+40%(F.P.)Rs.3974 =Rs.13,909 x 12 =Rs.1,66,908/-
per annum with multiplier of 18 = Rs.30,04,344/-deducted  personal expenses =Rs.15,02,172/-
Sandhya Bai vs Prakash on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72533535/
2 dependency amount Consortium to parents Rs. 44,000x2 =Rs.88,000/-
 Loss of estate Rs.16,500  Funeral expenses Rs.16,500/-

Total Amount Rs.16,23,172/-
3.

Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case as the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
The Tribunal has erred in assessing the income of the deceased as he was student of agricultural B.Tech Engineering, hence, prays for just and proper amount of compensation in the case.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company argued in support of the impugned award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case which does not call for any interference by this Court.
5. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellants.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, arguments made by the counsel for the appellants and the evidence that came on record, in the considered opinion of this Court, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be enhanced as under:
Income of deceased Rs.11,500/-+40%(F.P.)Rs.4600 =Rs.16,100/- pm -  personal expenses =Rs.8,050/-
 =Rs.17,38,800/- 
 amount  Consortium to parents Rs. 44,000x2 =Rs.88,
Loss of estate Rs.16,500
Funeral expenses Rs.16,500/-

Total Amount Rs.18,59,800/-
6.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.18,59,800/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.16,23,172/-.

Sandhya Bai vs Prakash on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72533535/
3
Accordingly, the appellants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.2,36,628/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.

7. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.
Rs.2,36,628/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.
9. In the result, the appeal is allowed in part and to the extent indicated herein above.

(ACHAL KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE RJ Sandhya Bai vs Prakash on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72533535/
